issues.description: is_registered mutation on shared TritonLoraConfig is racy and lacks a stated invariant for concurrent requests
issues.detail: Two concurrent first-time requests for the same LoRA both observe is_registered=False, both load .npy files, and both omit weights from later requests. The author has not stated the invariant guarding the cache-or-send decision. Either lock around the check-and-set, or always send weights, or document a single-writer invariant. State the invariant.

issues.description: Linear scan plus list-comprehension lookup of LoRA name is the wrong data structure
issues.detail: _get_lora_config and the two validators rebuild [c.name for c in lora_configs] and scan O(n) per request. A dict keyed by name was the natural choice from the start. The algorithm is fine; the data structure is paying interest. Store lora_configs as Dict[str, TritonLoraConfig] once at load time.

issues.description: task_id assignment is a global counter across repos with no termination or uniqueness proof
issues.detail: lora_task_id starts at 1 and increments across every repo and every multi_lora.json. The TRT-LLM contract for lora_task_id is not stated in the code; collisions across reloads, multiple models sharing a backend, or repeated _get_model_metadata calls are not analyzed. State the invariant: what makes a task_id unique, and over what scope.

issues.description: Bare except swallows ServerError siblings and returns None, hiding malformed configs
issues.detail: The outer except Exception catches anything that is not ServerError and returns None for the whole repo list, silently disabling LoRA. A reader cannot tell which failures are recoverable. Catch json.JSONDecodeError and OSError explicitly; let programming errors propagate. Also remove the debug print(traceback.format_exc()); logging belongs in a logger, not stdout.

issues.description: Variable shadowing of lora_config_path destroys readability
issues.detail: lora_config_path is bound to multi_lora.json at the top of the loop, then rebound to model.lora_config.npy inside the TRT-LLM branch. A careful reader following the code without running it cannot tell which path is live where. Rename the inner one (e.g., lora_config_npy_path). Code-as-literature: the names must not lie.

issues.description: Stray debug print and over-broad except-then-re-raise add noise without information
issues.detail: print(f"backend: {backend}") inside the per-LoRA loop and except ServerError as e: raise e are pure noise. The re-raise pattern is equivalent to not catching at all. Remove the print; drop the redundant ServerError branch. Literate code does not narrate to stdout.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED and WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE. The TRT-LLM LoRA path introduces a stateful is_registered flag on a shared config object with no concurrency invariant stated, a global incrementing task_id with no uniqueness scope stated, and a per-request linear scan over LoRA names that should be a dict lookup. Readability regressions (shadowed lora_config_path, stray prints, traceback dumps to stdout, redundant re-raise) further hurt the code-as-literature standard for foundational frontend code. The algorithm is essentially right; the analysis and the data structures need another pass before merge.
